news.text: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the ACL in his right knee in PSG's Champions League win over Barcelona on 20 October and is out for months after surgery.
Giorgi Kochorashvili is suspended after yellow cards against Hungary (2 Oct) and Northern Ireland (5 Oct).
Otar Kiteishvili is listed as missing. Karlobag reported a calf problem, and he also missed the October games.

Ramaz Svanadze, previously the Under-21 coach, replaced Willy Sagnol after the opening 0-1 home defeat to Northern Ireland in September (D2 L1 since). Georgia have failed to score in four straight games.

Rossi named a 27-man squad on 3 November. Roland Sallai, Barnabás Varga and Attila Szalai return from injury, and Milán Pető, Ákos Szendrei and József Urblík are new call-ups. Neither Sallai nor Varga played for Hungary in September or October.
Striker Milán Tóth misses out injured and is not in the FotMob squad list.

22Bet lists Dominik Szoboszlai as an injury doubt and Dániel Lukács as a fitness concern. Szoboszlai played 69 minutes for Liverpool at Crystal Palace on 8 November, and no other source mentions a problem.
Milos Kerkez served a one-match ban for two bookings against Ukraine on 5 October and is available again.

matches.context: Wales (3rd, 2-5) and Norway (4th, 6-8) are level on 3 points in Group A4, behind Portugal (12) and Denmark (6). Wales are ahead on head-to-head. The bottom side drops straight to League B and third goes into a relegation play-off, so this game probably decides which of the two avoids direct relegation. Wales won the reverse fixture 2-1 in Cardiff on 1 October: Oscar Bobb scored first, Daniel James equalised, Torbjørn Heggem was sent off on 46 minutes and Neco Williams won it with a free-kick.

news.text: Alexander Sørloth is recalled after missing the September and October windows with a muscle injury from pre-season.
Jørgen Strand Larsen withdrew and Erik Botheim was called up.
Haaland picked up a knock in the October defeat to Portugal but is fit. He and Ødegaard returned to training after missing a session, and Ødegaard is expected to start and captain.
Solbakken dropped Ørjan Nyland for Egil Selvik in the 4 October game in Porto, citing performance. SoccerNews expects Selvik to keep his place.
Torbjørn Heggem was sent off on 46 minutes in the reverse fixture. He is back in statz.ai's predicted XI.
Kieffer Moore has withdrawn from the squad injured.
Ben Cabango is suspended.
FootballPredictions.com also lists Sorba Thomas as suspended. No other source confirms it.
Harry Wilson (muscle injury, missed the four autumn games) and Joe Rodon (hamstring, out since August) are back in the squad.
Karl Darlow, Rubin Colwill and Kai Andrews are recalled and uncapped keeper Joe Duncan is called up. Jordan James, who started the reverse fixture, is not in the 26.

matches.context: Austria are unbeaten at the top of Group B3 on 8 points (9-5); a home win would clinch first place and promotion to League A with a game to spare. Ireland are third on 5 points, level with Kosovo (who beat them 1-0 in September) and three behind Austria, so they probably need to win in Linz and then beat Kosovo in Dublin to top the group. The reverse fixture in Dublin on 1 October ended 2-2: Troy Parrott scored twice (once from the penalty spot) before Alexander Prass and Michael Gregoritsch replied in the last 20 minutes.

news.text: Captain David Alaba is still out with a calf injury. Marco Friedl was moved to the standby list and Michael Svoboda called up.
Marko Arnautović has retired from international football and Marcel Sabitzer is on a planned break from the national team, so neither is available.
Christoph Baumgartner returns after a tendon injury. 17-year-old Sturm Graz midfielder Luca Weinhandl is in line for a debut.
22bet's preview lists Paul Wanner and Patrick Wimmer as out (Wanner hurt his foot against Kosovo in September). We found no second source for Wimmer.
Stefan Posch is in the predicted XIs, but statz.ai shows no Mainz appearance since 19 September and he missed both Kosovo games, so his match fitness is unverified.
Captain Nathan Collins returns from injury, Harvey Vale is back after rehab and Mark Travers returns in goal.
Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu misses out injured.
The squad is fully fit: everyone trained on Tuesday, assistant John O'Shea said. Séamus Coleman, without a club since leaving Everton, is with the squad in a hybrid coaching and playing role.
Evan Ferguson is not in the 24-man squad. Tom Cannon, Chiedozie Ogbene and Rocco Vata are the other forwards.

matches.context: Haiti's home leg is being played at Nu Stadium in Miami, home of Inter Miami, because the security situation means Haiti can't host. It is effectively a neutral venue in the US, near a big Haitian community. The second leg is in Cincinnati on 17 November, and the aggregate winner reaches the March 2027 Finals in Los Angeles and qualifies for the 2027 Gold Cup. Haiti were second in League A Group A on 9 points (W3 L1, 9-5), losing their last game 2-0 in Costa Rica. The US were seeded straight into the quarter-finals, won the last meeting 2-1 at the 2025 Gold Cup and have won the last three, each by one goal.

lineups.source: Sports Illustrated match preview (both XIs). CBS Sports' US XI agrees on nine outfield players.
lineups.alt: US: CBS Sports picks Matt Freese in goal and Sebastian Berhalter in midfield, with McKennie further forward and no Sullivan. Julian Hall is the alternative up front if Balogun is not fit enough to start. Haiti: the SI XI starts Delcroix and Duverne at centre-back, but FotMob lists Delcroix injured (leg, 1-2 weeks) and Covers lists Delcroix, Duverne and Metusala out, so the centre-back pair is uncertain. In September Sainté partnered Metusala there, and Sports Mole's October XI had Lacroix and Metusala. Sainté replaces the injured Bellegarde in midfield. Neither XI has been confirmed.

news.text: Spaniard David Badía, a former Barcelona academy and Almería coach, replaced Sébastien Migné after the World Cup. This is his first national-team job.
news.src: EFE via Diario El Mundo / MLSsoccer.com

news.text: Jean-Ricner Bellegarde, who scored in the 2-0 home win over Costa Rica, is out with a muscle injury.
Hannes Delcroix (leg injury, about 1-2 weeks) and Wilguens Paugain (day-to-day) are listed injured. Covers also lists centre-backs Jean-Kévin Duverne and Garven Metusala as out.
All-time leading scorer Duckens Nazon has missed the last two windows and his international future is unclear. FotMob lists him with a knock.
Ricardo Adé and Johny Placide have retired from international football. Alexandre Pierre is now the No. 1.
Haiti scored all nine group goals in their first three games and had no shot on target in the 2-0 defeat in Costa Rica.

Christian Pulisic returns after missing the four autumn friendlies with a microfracture of the right tibia and fibula, suffered in the World Cup last-16 defeat by Belgium. SI says he has scored in three of his last four games for Milan.
Folarin Balogun is recalled, but Pochettino says he "still isn't fully fit". All five of his Monaco appearances since his Everton move collapsed have come as a second-half substitute.
news.src: Fox Sports / AP via NBC Sports / CBS Sports

news.text: Weston McKennie is recalled after missing the autumn friendlies. CBS notes recent fitness issues.
Sergiño Dest left camp injured, and Gio Reyna, who started all four autumn friendlies, withdrew injured. Jack McGlynn was called up.
George Campbell (groin) withdrew and Mark McKenzie replaced him. Miles Robinson, Johnny Cardoso, Haji Wright, Alejandro Zendejas and Ricardo Pepi are injured and not in the squad.
news.src: SI / Fox Sports / AP via NBC Sports

news.text: Auston Trusty has missed club games since mid-October after his father's death but is expected to be available.
These are Pochettino's last two games in charge before he leaves for Manchester United. The No. 1 spot is open between Diego Kochen, Matt Freese and Brian Schwake.
Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and Justin Ellis scored six goals between them in the four autumn friendly wins over Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. Hall scored in each of his first three caps.
